summary: The 3GPP found cases where SIP private header fields (P-headers) from RFC 7315 need to appear in messages where RFC 7315 did not allow them. This informational document updates RFC 7315 to allow that, and it obsoletes RFC 7976.

plainLanguage.summary: Some special labels were only allowed on certain SIP messages. Mobile phone standards needed them on more messages, so the rules were relaxed. This memo says exactly which labels may now travel with which messages.

questions: what does rfc 9878 change in rfc 7315
subtitle: Loosens and corrects which SIP messages may carry the 3GPP private P-headers from RFC 7315.

tldr.problem: RFC 7315 contradicted itself about where SIP P-headers may appear, and the 3GPP found cases that need them in requests and responses where RFC 7315 did not allow them.
tldr.mechanism: This document replaces the usage statements in Section 5.7 of RFC 7315 with corrected text, for example allowing P-Access-Network-Info and P-Charging-Vector in ACK requests triggered by 2xx responses.
tldr.outcome: It updates RFC 7315 and obsoletes RFC 7976, whose change (P-Visited-Network-ID in responses) is carried forward.

facts.label: Header fields whose usage text changed

today: RFC 9878 is an Informational document that updates RFC 7315 and obsoletes RFC 7976, and no later RFC is recorded as replacing it. The change it carried forward from RFC 7976 is that any SIP response, except a 100 (Trying), may include a P-Visited-Network-ID header field.

sections.title: Introduction: Why the Rules Needed Fixing
sections.content:
The Third Generation Partnership Project has identified cases where different SIP private header extensions, referred to as P- header fields and defined in RFC 7315, need to be included in SIP requests and responses where they were not allowed according to that document. This document updates RFC 7315 in order to allow the affected header fields in such requests and responses, and it obsoletes RFC 7976. The changes related to RFC 7976 involve the inclusion of the P-Visited-Network-ID header field in SIP responses.

The document also makes updates to RFC 7315 in order to fix misalignments that occurred when RFC 3455 was updated and subsequently obsoleted by the publication of RFC 7315.

RFC 7315 contains contradictory statements about the usage of the P- header fields in SIP requests and responses, which leave the presence of these header fields open to interpretation and to different implementations. The statements in Section 5.7 of RFC 7315 are not aligned with the definitions and usage of the header fields specified in Section 4 of the same document. The document also notes one deliberate exception: allowing the P-Called-Party-ID header field in PUBLISH requests was done deliberately in RFC 7315, so it is not considered a misalignment.
sections.plainLanguage: RFC 7315 listed two different sets of rules for the same private headers, and the two sets did not agree. This memo picks one consistent set and fixes the wording.

sections.title: The Misalignments
sections.content:
Several updates are needed to fix the misalignments that occurred when RFC 3455 was obsoleted by RFC 7315. For P-Associated-URI, the statement that the header field can appear in the SIP REGISTER method is removed. For P-Called-Party-ID, the statement that the header field can appear in SIP responses is deleted, and a statement is added that it can appear in the SIP REFER method. For P-Access-Network-Info, a statement is added that the header field can appear in SIP responses. For P-Charging-Vector, a statement is added that the header field can appear in SIP responses, and a statement that it cannot appear in the SIP ACK method. For P-Charging-Function-Addresses, a statement is added that the header field can appear in SIP responses.

One further update clarifies usage compared with RFC 7315. For P-Visited-Network-ID, a statement is added that the header field cannot appear in the SIP NOTIFY, PRACK, INFO and UPDATE methods, and a statement that it can appear in all non-100 (Trying) responses.
sections.plainLanguage: Some headers were listed as allowed in one place and forbidden in another. The corrections remove the contradictions one header at a time.

sections.title: The 3GPP Use Cases
sections.content:
Two further updates are needed to implement the 3GPP use cases. For P-Access-Network-Info, a statement is added that the header field can appear in the SIP ACK method when triggered by a SIP 2xx response. For P-Charging-Vector, a statement is added that the header field can appear in the SIP ACK method when triggered by a SIP 2xx response.

The P-Access-Network-Info header field may contain the Network Provided Location Information, and a proxy in possession of appropriate information about the access technology might insert the header field with its own values, identified by the string network-provided defined in RFC 7315. Based on operator policy, roaming agreement, or both, the local time of the visited network may be included. The Call Data Records generated within the IP Multimedia Subsystem have to contain that location information in order to guarantee correct billing, and when an IMS session is modified the information also needs to be stored, because the location of the user at the time of the modification may generate a charging event. The information therefore has to be provided when the bearer establishment is triggered, at session release when the bearer deactivation is triggered, or when the bearer modification is triggered, for example a Quality of Service modification for a newly negotiated codec.

In some scenarios the bearer modification is triggered by the proxy upon reception of a Session Description Protocol answer within the SIP 2xx response to the SIP INVITE request, and in that case the information has to be provided within the SIP ACK request, which RFC 7315 did not allow. Upon reception of the answer, a proxy may therefore start procedures to obtain the information and include the header field in the ACK request. The header field shall not be included in ACK requests triggered by non-2xx responses.

The P-Charging-Vector header field carries an Inter Operator Identifier that lets the operators involved in a SIP dialog or transaction identify each other by exchanging operator identification information. In interconnection scenarios where one or more transit operators sit between the originating and terminating operator, the identities of the transit operators are represented by a transit-ioi parameter. Transit operators can be selected independently for each SIP method and direction of request, and a transit network has knowledge of only an individual request, so the selection can be an independent decision for each request, made on load, cost, percentage, time of day and other factors. For this reason the header field, which carries the transit information, has to be included in each SIP request and response, which RFC 7315 did not allow in the ACK request. A proxy that supports the extension and receives an ACK request may include the header field in it, and it shall not be included in ACK requests triggered by non-2xx responses.
sections.plainLanguage: Two headers carry information that the other end needs: the location of the user, so that the call can be billed correctly, and which operators are involved, so that each can be charged. Both are now allowed in the ACK that confirms a successful call.

sections.title: The Replacement Text for RFC 7315
sections.content:
Section 3 of the document contains the update to Section 5.7 of RFC 7315, implementing the misalignment fixes and the 3GPP requirements. The old text said that the P-Associated-URI header field can appear in the SIP REGISTER method and 2xx responses; that the P-Called-Party-ID header field can appear in the SIP INVITE, OPTIONS, PUBLISH, SUBSCRIBE and MESSAGE methods and all responses; that the P-Visited-Network-ID header field can appear in all SIP methods except ACK, BYE and CANCEL and all responses; that the P-Access-Network-Info header field can appear in all SIP methods except ACK and CANCEL; that the P-Charging-Vector header field can appear in all SIP methods except CANCEL; and that the P-Charging-Function-Addresses header field can appear in all SIP methods except ACK and CANCEL.

The new text says that the P-Associated-URI header field can appear in SIP REGISTER 2xx responses; that the P-Called-Party-ID header field can appear in the SIP INVITE, OPTIONS, PUBLISH, REFER, SUBSCRIBE and MESSAGE requests; that the P-Visited-Network-ID header field can appear in all SIP requests and the associated non-100 response message except in ACK, BYE, CANCEL, NOTIFY, PRACK, INFO and UPDATE; that the P-Access-Network-Info header field can appear in all SIP requests and the associated non-100 responses, except in CANCEL requests, CANCEL responses, and ACK methods triggered by non-2xx responses; that the P-Charging-Vector header field can appear in all SIP requests and the associated non-100 responses, except in CANCEL requests, CANCEL responses, and ACK requests triggered by non-2xx responses; and that the P-Charging-Function-Addresses header field can appear in all SIP methods and the associated non-100 responses, except in CANCEL requests, CANCEL responses, and ACK requests.
sections.plainLanguage: This section is the actual rule change: the six paragraphs above replace the six paragraphs in RFC 7315 that listed where each private header may appear.

sections.title: Security and Operational Considerations
sections.content:
The security considerations for these header fields are defined in RFC 7315. This specification allows some header fields to be present in messages where they were previously not allowed, and the security considerations and assumptions described in RFC 7315, such as regarding only sending information to trusted entities, also apply to those messages. The specification also disallows some header fields to be present in messages where they were previously allowed, which does not cause any security issues, but implementors need to be aware that implementations may not have been updated according to this document and take proper actions if a header field occurs, or does not occur, in a message where it should occur or should not occur.

The document adds the ability to include P-Access-Network-Info in ACK requests. As documented in RFC 7315, that header field may include privacy sensitive information, including the user's location, and the security and privacy considerations for it in ACK requests are similar to those for the other SIP requests discussed in Section 6.4 of RFC 7315. The security and privacy considerations for the P-Visited-Network-ID header field are similar to those for the other SIP responses discussed in Section 6.3 of RFC 7315.

The operational considerations note that the P- header fields are mainly used in, and in most cases only defined for, networks defined by the 3GPP, where the updates defined in this document are already defined, so the updates are not seen to cause backward-compatibility concerns. The document has no IANA actions, and the change since RFC 7976 is that any SIP response message, with the exception of a 100 (Trying) response, may include a P-Visited-Network-ID header field.
sections.plainLanguage: Loosening a rule can leak information, so the memo repeats the warning from RFC 7315 that these headers should only be sent to parties that are trusted. It also notes that the mobile networks already work this way, so nothing breaks in practice.

viz.caption: WHAT THE SIX PRIVATE HEADERS ARE FOR

items.title: P-Access-Network-Info
items.text: May carry Network Provided Location Information, and the local time of the visited network based on operator policy or roaming agreement.

items.title: P-Charging-Vector
items.text: Carries an Inter Operator Identifier so the operators involved can identify each other, plus a transit-ioi parameter naming the transit operators.

items.title: P-Visited-Network-ID
items.text: Names the visited network. May now appear in any SIP response except a 100 (Trying).

items.title: P-Associated-URI
items.text: May appear in SIP REGISTER 2xx responses only.

items.title: P-Called-Party-ID
items.text: May appear in the SIP INVITE, OPTIONS, PUBLISH, REFER, SUBSCRIBE and MESSAGE requests.

items.title: P-Charging-Function-Addresses
items.text: May appear in all SIP methods and the associated non-100 responses, except CANCEL and ACK requests.
